purpose: Frozen model configuration and pricing record for BM-06. Values here are configured, never fetched at run time; the two pre-execution checks below are re-confirmed immediately before execution and the run does not start if either fails.

model.dated_snapshot_variant: UNVERIFIED — establishing it is a provider request, which is not authorized
model.note: Selected 2026-08-19, replacing claude-sonnet-5. Under the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, extended thinking is on by default for Claude 5 models, its tokens are charged and counted against max_tokens, and the layer does not return them. Four of the five propose_change requests in the aborted preliminary run consumed the entire output allowance and emitted zero visible characters, at a 4,000-token cap and again at 8,000. reasoning_effort and response_format are both documented as ignored by that layer, so no OpenAI-shaped parameter reaches the behaviour; the only field that does is Anthropic-specific, and provider neutrality is an M1 acceptance property (M1-S03). Changing the model was the option that required no adapter change.

superseded.reason: default extended thinking exhausted the output allowance before any visible reply

provider.url_value: NOT_FROZEN — recorded at freeze time; HTTPS enforced by ProviderConfig.from_env
provider.note: No provider-specific header is sent to any host. Provider neutrality is an M1 acceptance property (M1-S03, test_adapter_neutrality.py) and is not relaxed for the benchmark.

temperature.resolution: post_chat takes temperature: float | None = None and omits the field entirely unless a caller passes one. Several current models reject a non-default sampling parameter outright and 0.0 is not the default anywhere, so asserting a preference nobody expressed was the defect. The fix was to stop sending it, not to branch on the provider.

superseded_claude_sonnet_5.note_verbatim: The $2/$10 per million input/output token pricing for Claude Sonnet 5, announced at launch as introductory pricing through August 31, 2026, is now the standard price. The previously scheduled increase to $3/$15 per million input/output tokens on September 1, 2026 will not occur.
superseded_claude_sonnet_5.recorded_disagreement: A reviewer reported on 2026-08-19 that the documentation still described $2/$10 as introductory with $3/$15 from 2026-09-01. The page fetched that day, and again on re-fetch, states the opposite. Retained because it explains why the ceiling changed; it is moot for this benchmark, which no longer uses that model.

pricing.tokenizer_note: The same page records that Claude 4.7 and later use a newer tokenizer producing about 30% more tokens for the same text, and that Sonnet 4.6 and earlier use the previous one. The input ceilings below are carried over unchanged from the claude-sonnet-5 configuration and are therefore, if anything, over-estimates for this model. Over-estimating a reservation is the safe direction.

worst_case_reservation.method: riftagent.records.reserve_cost at the frozen caps; token_ceiling = chars/3 + 1500
worst_case_reservation.note: The ceiling the SpendLedger reserves, not an expected spend. It assumes every prompt fills its context cap and every response fills its output cap, and that every arm-run needs its schema repair.
worst_case_reservation.repair_note: Every model operation carries the one schema-repair entitlement CLAUDE.md grants it, not propose_change alone (DAR-021). Each repair is reserved and settled under its own <operation>_repair key. A repair is made only for a completed reply that failed extraction or validation; a reply with finish_reason 'length' or no visible text is recorded as a failure and not repaired, because there is no completed response to re-serialise. Each repair reuses its operation's output cap. This ceiling assumes every arm-run needs every repair; none may.
worst_case_reservation.original_bm06_note: The 30-case BM-06 figures previously recorded here described a run that is NOT_RUN_PROTOCOL_INFEASIBLE and were computed at superseded rates without the repair request. They are removed rather than repriced: repricing them would present a ceiling for a run nobody can authorize as though it were current.

contingency.rule: The contingency is authorized separately and only if the primary run is invalidated. It is never silently consumed.
contingency.precedent: The M1a verify benchmark had a run invalidated by a harness defect: derive_judge_weakening built its diff with `git diff`, which compares the working tree to the index, so all four judge-weakening cases were malformed and that known-bad class measured nothing.
